claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

is_adopting.description: Whether the claimant is adopting the child.

child_has_moved_in.description: Whether the child being adopted has come to live with the claimant.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you'd like to claim Child Benefit for, and if so, how many children are there?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes, I'm asking about one child - my son Alex. He's 8 years old, and I'm actually in the process of adopting him. He hasn't come to live with me yet, but I'm helping to support him financially while the adoption goes through.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information about Alex. It's wonderful that you're going through the adoption process and supporting him financially.

To help me assess your eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to understand your situation a bit better:

**Has Alex come to live with you yet, or is he still living elsewhere while the adoption process is ongoing?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't come to live with me yet. He's still living elsewhere while we're going through the adoption process. But I am contributing towards his upkeep - I help out financially with things he needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I understand Alex hasn't moved in with you yet while the adoption is being finalized.

According to the Child Benefit rules, you can claim Child Benefit as soon as a child you're adopting comes to live with you - you don't have to wait until the adoption process is complete. However, the key requirement is that the child needs to be living with you.

Since Alex hasn't come to live with you yet, let me ask:

**Do you know approximately when Alex is expected to come and live with you?**

Also, it's worth noting that you might be able to get Child Benefit for a period before the adoption in certain circumstances. Once Alex does come to live with you, you would be able to claim Child Benefit from that point, even while the adoption process is still ongoing.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
I'm not entirely sure of the exact timing yet - these things can take a while with all the paperwork and assessments. It could still be a few months before he moves in with me.

So just to be clear - even though I'm paying towards his costs now, around £30 a week for things he needs, I wouldn't be able to claim until he's actually living with me?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that clarification. Yes, that's correct based on the standard rules - you would normally be able to claim Child Benefit from the point when Alex comes to live with you, even if the adoption process isn't yet complete.

However, the rules do mention that "You might be able to get Child Benefit for a period before the adoption" in certain circumstances. Since you're already contributing financially to Alex's upkeep while waiting for him to move in, there may be some exceptions that could apply to your situation.

Let me ask you a couple more questions to get a complete picture:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I think that covers everything. So what does this mean for me right now? Can I claim or do I need to wait?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on my assessment of your situation with Alex, here's what this means for you:

**Current Situation:**
Under the standard Child Benefit rules, you would normally need to wait until Alex comes to live with you before you can claim Child Benefit. Once he does move in with you, you'll be eligible to claim immediately - you won't need to wait for the adoption to be finalized.

**However, there may be an exception:**
The rules do mention that you "might be able to get Child Benefit for a period before the adoption," but the specific criteria for this aren't spelled out in the standard guidance. Given that you're already contributing £30 per week towards Alex's upkeep during the adoption process, you might qualify under this exception.

**My recommendation:**
I'd strongly encourage you to **contact the Child Benefit Office directly** to discuss your specific circumstances. They can assess whether your situation qualifies for Child Benefit before Alex moves in with you, based on the financial support you're providing during the adoption process.

You'll definitely be eligible once Alex comes to live with you, so at that point you should claim right away - don't wait for the adoption to be complete. But it's worth checking with the Child Benefit Office now to see if you can claim even sooner given your current contributions.
